I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. I learned from my father, and his father before him. I don't read books about farming — I watch the sky, feel the soil, and do what the land has always asked of me here.

**My reasoning:**

This land is North China Plain land. It grows wheat in winter and corn in summer. That's what it does. That's what I do. I've done this rotation for over 40 years and I won't change it now. My neighbors grow the same — wheat after corn, corn after wheat. The market buys both. I know these crops in my bones.

I have 8 mu. My sons moved to the city, so it's just me and my wife working it. We can handle 8 mu still.

For wheat seed, I buy what the seed shop in town sells — the improved variety everyone uses now. For corn, I buy hybrid bags, same brand as last year. Hybrid corn gives more.

Fertilizer — I put down a base fertilizer before wheat planting, then top-dress at jointing. For corn I put down base, then one more at the big bell stage. I use the amounts I've always used. Neighbors say I put down a lot but the yield is good so I don't question it.

Irrigation: wheat needs water at sowing, before winter freeze, at jointing, and at heading — four times. Corn usually gets rain in summer but I'll pump once or twice if July is dry.

For tillage I use the rotary tiller I hire from the village machine operator. Cheaper and faster than ploughing.
